clue.text: Including what accounts for 50% of assets in total makes sense

indicators.note: including something means taking it inside, so one piece sits within the phrase for total

blocks.note: to total figures is to add them up
three of the six letters in assets are S, so S makes up half of it

explanation.surface: An accountant checks that the books balance once half the assets are included in the total.
explanation.walkthrough: The 50% is not half of the word taken off one end: it is the single letter that fills three of the six places in assets.
explanation.definitionFit: When an argument adds up it is logical and coherent, which is what we mean when something makes sense.

clue.text: Neglected state of son adopted by dreadful couple

indicators.note: a child adopted by a couple is taken into their family, so one piece is taken inside the other

blocks.note: dire means dreadful
S is the standard abbreviation for son
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: A sorry tale of a boy taken in by an awful pair of parents.
explanation.walkthrough: The son's letter lands between the two words for dreadful and couple, splitting the first of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A building in disrepair has been allowed to decay through lack of upkeep and maintenance.

clue.text: Traces dictator's money to America

indicators.note: someone dictating says words out loud for another to write, so we want what the following words sound like

blocks.note: cents are small US coins, money in America

explanation.surface: Investigators follow the trail of a tyrant's funds to the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' looks like a tyrant but is just someone speaking aloud for a typist.
explanation.definitionFit: Scents are the faint smells a hound follows, so they are traces or trails left behind.

clue.text: College is spreading these people's belief system

indicators.note: spreading out scatters things, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a type of college
taken as written
them refers to a group of people

explanation.surface: A college is said to be propagating some group's creed.
explanation.walkthrough: A polytechnic was a type of British college, POLY for short.
explanation.definitionFit: Polytheism is worship of many gods, a religious belief system.

clue.text: Request for more ends in sale to sadistic bloke in Oliver Twist

indicators.note: we keep only the final letter from each of the words that follow
a twist bends things out of shape, so the collected letters are rearranged

blocks.note: final letter
final letter
final letter
final letter
final letter
final letter

explanation.surface: Oliver Twist famously asked for more, and the reader thinks of Bumble or Sikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oliver Twist' is not the novel at all: Oliver gives its last letter and Twist is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience shouting encore is calling for the performers to give them another piece.

clue.text: Eat out and so forth with husband

blocks.note: etc. is the abbreviation for et cetera, and so forth
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Dining at a restaurant and doing other things with one's spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat out' reads like going to a restaurant but means corrode, as acid does a metal plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to corrode a surface with acid, eating away at it to cut a design.

clue.text: Talk briefly with outspoken clergyman

indicators.note: kept brief, the word is cut short by dropping its last letter

blocks.note: to chat is to talk
plain-spoken, frank

explanation.surface: Having a quick word with a blunt member of the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a member of the clergy attached to a regiment, college, hospital or prison.

clue.text: Control assumed by princeling ultimately?

indicators.note: to assume something is to take it on, so one word takes the other inside it

blocks.note: a rein is a means of control
ultimately points to the final letter

explanation.surface: A young prince may one day take on power.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a princeling will ultimately assume the throne's control. 'ultimately' also selects the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A reign is a monarch's period of rule, the control a prince inherits when he finally takes the throne.

clue.text: Thoughtless young woman weighed down by remorse on vacation

indicators.note: a vacated word is emptied of its contents, leaving only the outside letters
in a down entry something weighed down sits beneath, so this piece comes after the other

blocks.note: first and last letters only
a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: An inconsiderate girl is burdened with guilt while on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Being remiss means careless and negligent of one's duty, failing to give proper thought.

clue.text: Come to an agreement to lower pay

blocks.note: first meaning: resolve a dispute
second meaning: clear a bill

explanation.surface: Unions and bosses reach a deal to cut wages.
explanation.definitionFit: Parties settle a dispute by reaching terms, and a customer settles an account by paying what is owed.

clue.text: Soldiers certain to suppress mass resistance and succeed

indicators.note: suppressed letters are kept out of sight, so they are removed from the words

blocks.note: soldiers as opposed to officers are the men
sure means certain
M is the symbol for mass in physics
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Troops confident of crushing a popular uprising and winning.
explanation.walkthrough: M comes out of MEN and R comes out of SURE. 'Mass resistance' reads as a popular revolt but is two physics symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed in the sense of follow after is to ensue, as consequences come after an event.

clue.text: Vital cure could be financially rewarding

indicators.note: what the letters could be once rearranged into another word

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A life-saving drug could make its maker rich.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucrative business produces plenty of profit, so it pays well in money terms.

clue.text: I'd spelt out fully who I am

blocks.note: ID is the short form; written in full it is the word it abbreviates

explanation.surface: Someone spells their name out in full to prove who they are.
explanation.walkthrough: I'd looks like 'I would' but is ID, the standard short form, so writing it out in full gives the whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: Your identity is the fact of being a particular person, the answer to the question of your name and self.

clue.text: Tree trunk almost entirely hidden in earth?

indicators.note: if a word is nearly all concealed only its opening letter shows

blocks.note: the plane is a tree common in city streets
only the opening letter stays visible

explanation.surface: A tree with its trunk nearly buried in soil.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks earth as an example: it is one planet among several.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earth is a planet, so the answer is defined by example, with the question mark flagging that.

clue.text: Animal adapting to change around North America

indicators.note: the letters are made to change their order

blocks.note: taken as written
NA is the abbreviation for North America

explanation.surface: A creature evolving to suit a new environment across a continent.
explanation.walkthrough: All ten letters are rearranged together; around just joins the second piece on.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda is a black-and-white bear of China, an animal by any measure.

clue.text: I've got the same picture!

blocks.note: first meaning: the call in a children's card game when two matching cards turn up
second meaning: a quick photograph

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue sounds like a player spotting matching picture cards, which is when the call is made.
explanation.definitionFit: Players cry snap on matching cards, and a snapshot or snap is an informal photograph.

clue.text: Authentic revolutionary zeal's capable of surviving imprisoning

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the word for zeal is read backwards
to imprison is to shut inside, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: viable means able to live or survive
fire is passion, ardour

explanation.surface: A genuine radical's enthusiasm survives even prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' sits beside zeal like a political label, but it is the signal to turn the word for zeal round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something verifiable can be confirmed true, which loosely makes it genuine or authentic.

clue.text: Striking university dons see about working

indicators.note: working letters are set in motion and rearranged

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: University lecturers on strike look into getting back to work.
explanation.walkthrough: Striking, dons and working all suggest an industrial dispute at a college; striking means good-looking, and the dons are only a verb meaning puts on.
explanation.definitionFit: Beauteous is a poetic word for beautiful, and striking good looks are just that.

clue.text: King engulfed by allegations as fighting mounts

indicators.note: something engulfed is swallowed up, so it ends inside the other word

blocks.note: charges are accusations
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is swamped by accusations as conflict escalates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighting mounts' looks like a verb phrase, conflict increasing, but mounts is a noun: horses ridden into battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Chargers are war horses, the steeds knights rode into battle.

clue.text: This kind of power you are reportedly in pursuit of?

indicators.note: reported words are heard rather than seen, so we take the sound of the phrase before it

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
two letters that say the phrase, as in a text message
chasing means pursuing

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what sort of force someone is after.
explanation.walkthrough: Power does double duty: it is part of the definition and also gives its symbol P.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchasing power is the amount money can buy, so this word names that kind of power.

clue.text: Confusion surrounds informer operating illegally

indicators.note: to surround is to enclose, so the word for confusion goes round the other piece

blocks.note: in printing, pie is type that has been jumbled up
a rat is someone who informs on others

explanation.surface: Chaos breaks out around a grass running an illegal racket.
explanation.walkthrough: Pie, also spelt pi, is an old printers' word for a muddle of type. A grass is British slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate radio station broadcasts without a licence, so as an adjective the word means operating unlawfully.

clue.text: Vacillate endlessly and move from side to side

indicators.note: without its end, the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: to waver is to vacillate

explanation.surface: Someone dithering forever and swaying back and forth.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands and flags wave by swinging to and fro, which is moving from side to side.

clue.text: Maintained circulation as newspaper boss stopped working

blocks.note: ED is short for editor
a machine that has died has stopped working

explanation.surface: A paper kept its readership going when its editor broke down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circulation' looks like a newspaper's sales; here it is water swirling round.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that eddied swirled round in a circular current, keeping up a circular motion.

clue.text: What links provide following drive for party members

blocks.note: first meaning: on a golf course, the putting surfaces a player reaches after teeing off
second meaning: members of an environmental political party

explanation.walkthrough: Links are golf courses by the sea, and a drive is the long opening shot from the tee.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers putt out on greens after their drives, and members of the Green Party are known as Greens.

clue.text: What guides prayers of Catholic woman who's lost heart?

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letters of the name are taken out

blocks.note: a woman's name

explanation.surface: Asking what keeps a disheartened Catholic woman praying.
explanation.walkthrough: The two central letters EM are removed from the name ROSEMARY.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosary is a string of beads Catholics count while saying a set sequence of prayers.

clue.text: Say when northbound train's beginning to enter platform

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter alone
entering means going inside, so this letter goes into another word
in a down entry, heading north means reading upwards, so the letters run in the opposite order

blocks.note: e.g. stands for for example, which is say
as in as I arrived, meaning when
the opening letter

explanation.surface: Telling someone when the northbound train is about to pull into the platform.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, northbound means the finished string is read from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage is a raised platform on which actors perform.

clue.text: Newspaper article about judge had an effect

indicators.note: the newspaper piece goes round the other word

blocks.note: an op-ed is an opinion piece on the page opposite the editorial
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A newspaper column about a judge made an impact.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule that operated was in force and working, so it had an effect.

clue.text: What predicts recurring feature of momentary phenomena?

indicators.note: a feature is a part of something, and recurring says the same letters turn up in each of the next words

blocks.note: the letters sit inside the first word, and again inside the second

explanation.surface: Asking what forecasts fleeting events.
explanation.walkthrough: The same four letters lie in mOMENtary and again in phenOMENa, hence recurring.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign believed to foretell the future, so it is something that predicts.

clue.text: Shopkeeper deals with staff

blocks.note: to trade is to deal
to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: A retailer handles their employees.
explanation.walkthrough: Staff looks like a noun, employees, but it is the verb, as in to man a desk.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman can mean a person who keeps a shop and sells goods, a retailer.

clue.text: Express strong feelings about e-book

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the following letters are read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: Someone getting passionate over digital books.
explanation.walkthrough: The e of e-book is taken as a letter; E TOME is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To emote is to show emotion in an exaggerated, theatrical way.

clue.text: Smaller amount supported by class action

indicators.note: supported from beneath, this piece comes first with the other after it

blocks.note: less means a smaller amount
on means in action, operating

explanation.surface: A smaller sum backed by a group lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class action' looks like a group lawsuit; class is the definition (a lesson) and action gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson is a period of teaching in school, and class is a common synonym for it.

clue.text: Musician wanting leader of band's help

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the word is missing a letter
the leader of a word is the letter at its front

blocks.note: a bass player
leader of band is its first letter

explanation.surface: A player from a group needs its frontman's support.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to give someone aid, so it means help as a verb or noun.
